title: 7. Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Relative Multiples
summary: At $443.59 ($153.77B market cap, ~$147.0B–$149.8B EV), ISRG trades at 35.52x Forward P/E and 42.74x P/FCF—pricing in 16.89%–18.35% 10-year FCF CAGR off audited FY2025 FCF ($2,491.2M) at 8.5%–9.0% WACC, while a 28.0x Forward P/E stress test ($370.72–$395.08) shows why chasing $443.59 lacks margin of safety.

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; implied expectations are what you underwrite.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: 7.1 Valuation Snapshot & Why the Stock De-Rated 26.5% From Its High

At the November 13, 2026 close of $443.59, Intuitive carries a $153.77 billion market cap across 346.60 million shares [22]. Subtracting $6.80 billion of Q3 2026 cash and investments against zero debt yields an enterprise value (EV) near $146.97 billion [3, 22]. (Finviz lists $149.83 billion EV using $11.75/share, or ~$4.07 billion, in short-term cash [22].) On TTM sales of $11.58 billion (+20.45% YoY) and a 32.25% operating margin, ISRG trades at 53.67x TTM P/E ($8.27 EPS) and 35.52x Forward P/E [22]. It also trades at 33.26x EV/EBITDA, 12.94x EV/Sales, 42.74x P/FCF, and 9.62x P/B [22].

Those multiples reflect a major valuation reset over the past year. ISRG fell 21.56% over the trailing 12 months (-21.68% YTD) and sits 26.54% below its $603.88 peak, even as TTM sales grew 20.45% and Non-GAAP margins rose [13, 14, 22]. Three drivers compressed the multiple from >70x trailing earnings down to 35.52x forward earnings. First, U.S. da Vinci case growth slowed to ~10% YoY in Q3 2026 under GLP-1 weight-loss drugs and expiring ACA subsidies [13, 14]. Second, tariffs took 65–120 bps out of gross margin [4]. Third, risk-free yields jumped, with the 10-year Treasury at 5.10% and the 2-year at 4.86% on November 12, 2026 [26].

Importantly, this de-rating happened right as capital intensity fell [1, 2]. Intuitive spent $1,064.2 million on CapEx in FY2023 and $1,111.2 million in FY2024 to expand plants in Sunnyvale, Mexicali, Germany, and Bulgaria, before CapEx dropped to $539.8 million in FY2025 [1, 2]. Operating cash flow hit $3,197.0 million in 9M 2026 alone, lifting implied TTM free cash flow to ~$3.60 billion ($153.77B market cap / 42.74x P/FCF) [3, 22]. Management also spent $2.94 billion on buybacks in Q3 2026, retiring shares straight into the valuation reset [3].
7.2 Reverse DCF: What Growth Rate Is Priced In at $443.59?

Instead of relying on one point-estimate DCF, we invert the math. We solve for the 10-year Free Cash Flow (FCF) CAGR needed to justify Intuitive's ~$147.0 billion EV today. Because CapEx normalized in FY2025 after the $2.18 billion plant buildout in FY2023–FY2024 [1], the choice of base-year FCF changes the implied growth hurdle:

web_blocks.takeaway: Anchored on audited FY2025 FCF ($2,491.2M), $443.59 requires 16.89%–18.35% 10-year FCF compounding at 8.5%–9.0% WACC (20.54% at 9.5% WACC). Using implied TTM FCF ($3,598.0M = $153.77B / 42.74x P/FCF) lowers the hurdle to 12.15%–13.52%, though 9M 2026 CapEx is not yet audited.

web_blocks.html: We anchor our primary Reverse DCF on audited FY2025 FCF ($2,491.2M) [1]. At an 8.5%–9.0% WACC (5.10% 10-year Treasury yield [26] plus 3.40%–3.90% equity risk premium) and 3.5% terminal growth, $443.59 prices in 16.89%–18.35% annual FCF growth for 10 years (rising to 20.54% at 9.5% WACC). That hurdle sits above consensus 16.26% five-year EPS growth [22]. By contrast, an implied TTM FCF figure of $3,598.0M ($153.77B market cap / 42.74x P/FCF) implies a lower 12.15%–13.52% CAGR at 8.5%–9.0% WACC [22]. Because 9M 2026 CapEx is not separately broken out in the earnings release, $3,598.0M remains an implied portal figure rather than an audited cash-flow base.
7.3 Historical Valuation Bands & 28.0x Forward P/E De-Rating Stress Test

Over the past five years, ISRG traded at 38x to 65x Forward P/E, 11x to 20x EV/Sales, and 40x to 80x P/FCF. At 35.52x Forward P/E and 12.94x EV/Sales, ISRG sits near the bottom quartile of its 5-year range [22]. Its 2.18x PEG ratio (against 16.26% 5-year EPS growth) also sits below its 2.5x–3.2x median [22]. If EPS compounds 15%–17% annually over two years and the multiple holds 36x–38x, the Base Target hits $515.00 (+16.1%).

However, a 28.0x Forward P/E De-Rating Stress Test exposes why chasing $443.59 lacks margin of safety. Applying 28.0x to NTM EPS—from $13.24 (+6% growth) to $14.11 (Base)—yields $370.72 to $395.08. That represents -10.9% to -16.4% downside from $443.59 and breaches our $401.77 hard stop. In a 5.10% 10-year Treasury and S&P 500 Correction regime [26], paying 35.52x forward earnings leaves too little buffer. Waiting for the $418.34–$431.08 support zone restores 2.86:1–5.83:1 asymmetry.

book_subsections.title: What $443.59 Actually Buys: Deconstructing the Multiple Reset
paragraphs: When a premier compounder drops 26.5 percent from its 52-week high while its top line is still expanding above 20 percent, you and I have to ask whether the market has uncovered a structural crack or simply repriced duration. At the November 13, 2026 close of $443.59, Intuitive Surgical commands a $153.77 billion market capitalization and roughly $147.0 billion in enterprise value net of its $6.80 billion Q3 2026 cash and investment hoard, with zero funded debt on the balance sheet. Note that standard financial portals such as Finviz report an enterprise value of $149.83 billion because they deduct only short-term cash and equivalents of roughly $4.07 billion, whereas the Q3 2026 balance sheet holds $6.80 billion including long-term marketable securities. Either way, we are looking at an unlevered $147 billion to $150 billion enterprise.

On trailing twelve-month revenue of $11.58 billion and a 32.25 percent operating margin, the stock trades at 53.67 times trailing earnings, 35.52 times forward earnings, 33.26 times EV/EBITDA, 12.94 times EV/Sales, and 42.74 times free cash flow. Those numbers look rich only until you compare them to Intuitive's own history and to the macro backdrop. Over the past five years, Intuitive routinely traded between 38 and 65 times forward earnings, with a PEG ratio median between 2.5 and 3.2 times. Today's 35.52 times forward multiple and 2.18 times PEG ratio sit near the bottom quartile of that range.

Why did the multiple compress from over 70 times trailing earnings at the peak down to 35.5 times forward earnings today? Three transparent forces did the work. First, U.S. da Vinci procedure growth cooled to roughly 10 percent in Q3 2026 as GLP-1 weight-loss drugs dampened bariatric surgery volume and expiring ACA subsidies created uncertainty around elective hospital utilization. Second, tariff costs trimmed 65 to 120 basis points from gross margin. Third, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.10 percent, raising the discount rate on all long-duration cash flows. Crucially, none of these forces broke Intuitive's clinical moat or installed-base economics.

Even more revealing is how Intuitive's enterprise-value-to-sales and free-cash-flow multiples behave across market cycles. Over the past five years, investors paid between 11 and 20 times enterprise value to sales and between 40 and 80 times free cash flow to own this franchise. At 12.94 times EV/Sales and 42.74 times P/FCF today, you are buying Intuitive near the exact valuation floor that historically preceded multi-year outperformance whenever procedure fears subsided. Meanwhile, Wall Street's 1.82 consensus recommendation score and $492.90 average price target reflect steady institutional sponsorship without euphoric sell-side crowding—leaving meaningful room for positive earnings revisions as da Vinci 5 software and Force Feedback adoption scale.

book_subsections.title: The Reverse DCF Verdict: 16.89%–18.35% Off Audited FY2025 FCF vs. Implied TTM Math
paragraphs: Rather than building a fragile spreadsheet to prove a preconceived price target, let us flip the math around and ask what $443.59 requires Intuitive Surgical to deliver over the next decade. Anchoring on audited FY2025 free cash flow of $2,491.2 million, an 8.5% to 9.0% WACC (built from the 5.10% 10-year Treasury yield) and 3.5% terminal growth require 16.89% to 18.35% annual FCF compounding for ten straight years. That hurdle rises to 20.54% at a 9.5% WACC and sits above consensus 16.26% five-year EPS growth.

By contrast, an implied trailing twelve-month FCF figure of $3,598.0 million—derived from $153.77 billion market cap divided by Finviz's 42.74x P/FCF—lowers the 10-year hurdle to 12.15%–13.52% at 8.5%–9.0% WACC. Because 9M 2026 CapEx is not separately broken out in the quarterly release, $3,598.0 million is an implied figure rather than an audited base. That distinction matters: at $443.59, investors are still underwriting upper-teens compounding off audited FY2025 cash flows.

Put those two numbers side by side against Intuitive's actual operating history. From FY2016 through FY2025, revenue compounded at 15.7% annually and audited free cash flow rose from $1,000.0 million to $2,491.2 million (a 10.7% nine-year CAGR that included the 2023–2024 plant buildout before surging 91.1% in FY2025). Trailing twelve-month sales grew 20.45%, and consensus models 16.26% annual EPS growth over the next five years. In other words, 16.89% to 18.35% FCF compounding off FY2025's base is achievable if da Vinci 5 and Ion scale smoothly, yet it leaves zero room for a U.S. procedure miss at $443.59.

book_subsections.title: Why Intuitive Trades at a Premium to Stryker, Medtronic, and Boston Scientific
paragraphs: A glance at the peer table explains why value screens often misread Intuitive Surgical. Stryker trades at 18.99 times forward earnings and 16.97 times EV/EBITDA; Medtronic trades at 16.08 times forward earnings and 14.54 times EV/EBITDA; Boston Scientific trades at 14.20 times forward earnings and 12.74 times EV/EBITDA; and Johnson & Johnson trades at 24.65 times forward earnings. On the surface, Intuitive's 35.52 times forward multiple looks expensive against the large-cap medical technology group.

Yet look under the hood at the economic engine. Intuitive is growing trailing revenue at 20.45 percent—more than double Stryker's 7.87 percent, Medtronic's 9.77 percent, Boston Scientific's 8.88 percent, and Johnson & Johnson's 7.81 percent. Its 32.25 percent operating margin clears those peers by 640 to 1,232 basis points, its 18.50 percent return on invested capital is roughly double Medtronic's 6.90 percent and Stryker's 9.54 percent, and it carries zero debt compared to 0.47 to 0.66 debt-to-equity across large-cap medtech. Meanwhile, pure-play surgical robotics challenger PROCEPT BioRobotics trades at 3.49 times EV/Sales because it posts a negative 33.61 percent operating margin and negative 28.48 percent ROIC. You pay a higher multiple for Intuitive because you are buying unlevered, high-margin, 84 percent recurring monopoly cash flows.

book_subsections.title: CapEx Normalization, Buyback Math, and the Margin of Safety
paragraphs: One of the most overlooked drivers in Intuitive Surgical's valuation today is the simple arithmetic of capital expenditure normalization and opportunistic share repurchases. Between 2022 and 2024, Intuitive invested heavily in expanding its physical manufacturing footprint across Sunnyvale, Mexicali, Germany, and Bulgaria so it could support multi-year da Vinci 5 and Ion unit scaling without repeating the component bottlenecks of 2022. Capital expenditures jumped from $532.4 million in 2022 to $1,064.2 million in 2023 and $1,111.2 million in 2024. While that buildout was underway, free cash flow temporarily compressed to $749.8 million in 2023 and $1,303.8 million in 2024, making headline price-to-free-cash-flow multiples look artificially elevated.

Once those campuses came online, capital expenditures dropped by more than half to $539.8 million in 2025, unleashing a 91 percent jump in free cash flow to $2,491.2 million. Over the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow accelerated further to $3,197.0 million, supporting an implied trailing twelve-month FCF near $3,598.0 million ($153.77B / 42.74x P/FCF). Rather than sitting passively on Treasury bills, Intuitive stepped into the 2026 stock pullback and repurchased $2.94 billion of its own shares in Q3 alone, ending September 30, 2026 with $6.80 billion in cash and investments and zero debt.

Even with that cash-flow cushion, our 28.0x Forward P/E de-rating stress test shows why chasing $443.59 in a 5.10% 10-year Treasury and Correction regime lacks margin of safety. Applying 28.0x to NTM EPS ($13.24 at +6% growth to $14.11 Base) yields $370.72 to $395.08—a -10.9% to -16.4% drop that breaches our $401.77 hard stop. Waiting for a pullback into the $418.34–$431.08 support zone restores a true margin of safety.

To see why that patience pays, compare the risk-reward math at $443.59 versus $431.08 or $418.34. At $443.59, your upside to our $515.00 Base Target is $71.41 per share against $41.82 of downside to our $401.77 stop, a 1.71-to-1 ratio that leaves little cushion if the S&P 500 Correction deepens or 10-year yields push higher. By contrast, entering at $431.08 raises upside to $83.92 against $29.31 of stop risk—a 2.86-to-1 payoff—and entering near $418.34 lifts it to 5.83-to-1. In a 5.10 percent risk-free yield environment, demanding at least 2.86-to-1 asymmetry on a Tier 3 setup protects capital while keeping you positioned for da Vinci 5's multi-year upgrade cycle.

Under a 28.0x Forward P/E stress test ($13.24–$14.11 NTM EPS), fair value drops to $370.72–$395.08 (-10.9% to -16.4%), breaching the $401.77 stop and favoring patience for $418.34–$431.08 support.
